title: The Hydrogen Atom, Honestly
blurb: One electron, one proton, and every liberty taken with the picture.

steps.title: Start with the only atom that can be solved
body: One electron, one proton, and a potential that goes as 1 over r. This is the last atom in the periodic table with a closed-form answer, and everything coming up is that answer rather than a fit to it.
The cloud is a hundred thousand points drawn from the exact probability density. Nothing here was tuned to look right.

steps.title: A probability, not a shell
body: There is no orbit and no surface. The electron has a probability of turning up anywhere, and the cloud is that probability drawn as density.

The nucleus is at true scale now, which is why you cannot see it. At this magnification a proton is well under a pixel across, and the marker shown by default is a labelled visual liberty rather than a size.

steps.title: n sets the size, l sets the shape
body: Same n, different l. The 2s is a ball with a gap inside it, the 2p is two lobes, and that gap is a real node: a surface where the electron is never found.
The mean radius moves too. The 2s sits at 318 pm and the 2p at 265 pm, so the rounder state is also the bigger one.

steps.title: Same energy, different shape
body: Those two states look nothing alike, and they sit at exactly the same -3.40 eV. Nothing about their shapes says they should.

This is the accidental degeneracy, and accidental is the right word: it belongs to the 1 over r potential and to nothing else. Put a second electron in the way to screen the nucleus and it breaks immediately, which is why no other atom can show you this.

steps.title: m, and a basis is a choice
body: The chemistry orbitals you were taught, p_x and p_y, are not more real than the complex states with definite m. They are sums of them, and which set you call the answer is a choice of basis rather than a fact about the atom.
Both are first-class here, and the badge says which one is on screen. Switch it and watch the same physics wear a different face.

steps.title: A surface is a contour, not a boundary
body: Textbook orbital pictures draw a surface and leave you to assume the electron is inside it. This one encloses 90% of the electron, and says so, because the other 10% is genuinely outside and goes on forever.
Drag the fraction and the surface breathes in and out. There is no radius at which the atom stops.

steps.title: So the degeneracy was the model's lie
body: Turn on fine structure and the level drawn as one line becomes several. The 2s and the 2p were never exactly equal. The model that said so had left three things out.
The badge changes from EXACT to APPROXIMATION, and it names what is missing rather than implying nothing is. This is an alpha-squared perturbation, correct to that order and no further.

steps.title: Dirac, exactly, and the gap it still leaves
body: The Dirac equation solves hydrogen in closed form, relativity included, so the badge goes back to EXACT. It gives the fine structure the perturbation was approximating.

It is still not the measured answer. Here the 2s and 2p at the same j come out exactly degenerate, and the laboratory disagrees. That difference is the Lamb shift. It is not modelled, and saying so beats quietly closing the gap.

steps.title: Levels become lines
body: Every arrow between two levels is a photon, and its wavelength is fixed by the gap. The 2 to 1 transition comes out at 121.57 nm and the 3 to 2 at 656.47 nm, the red line in every hydrogen discharge tube you have seen.
The dots on the axis are vendored NIST measurements, not a fit. The residual panel shows the computed lines agreeing with them, which is the only reason to believe anything above.

steps.title: What the picture cost
body: Every badge on this screen is a claim about how much to trust what sits next to it. EXACT means the stated model was solved in closed form. APPROXIMATION means the assumptions are named. VISUAL LIBERTY means the choice was presentational, and disclosed anyway.

The nucleus marker is a liberty. The colour map is a liberty. The point size is a liberty. None of them changes a number, and all of them are labelled, because a picture that hides its choices is a picture you cannot check.
